interest: This document provides archival evidence of the growing naval contacts and official courtesies between Imperial Japan and Nazi Germany in mid-1937, following the signing of the Anti-Comintern Pact in late 1936. Specifically, it highlights U.S. military and diplomatic monitoring of the visit by the Japanese heavy cruiser Ashigara to the German naval port of Kiel following its participation in King George VI's Coronation Naval Review. It also demonstrates State Department registry practices, showing how U.S. Naval Attaché intelligence reports were tracked and cross-referenced within the diplomatic decimal filing system.
overview: This file consists of a U.S. State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.3362, titled 'Visits of vessels, hydroplanes, dirigibles of Japan to ports of Germany.' The sheet indexes two records from mid-1937 documenting Japanese naval visits to German ports. The first entry, dated June 28, 1937, from the Navy Department, references a Naval Attaché report concerning courtesies and privileges accorded to naval officers of the Japanese cruiser Ashigara (transcribed in the record as 'ASHICA-A') during its visit to Kiel. The second entry, dated May 27, 1937, notes Naval Attaché Germany Report #R-361 concerning visits of Japanese naval vessels to German ports, with a cross-reference to another decimal file.

subfiles.about: A State Department index sheet recording papers filed under classification 894.3362 regarding visits of Japanese naval vessels to German ports in 1937.
subfiles.summary: This index sheet catalogs two communications received by the Department of State in 1937 under classification 894.3362. The first entry, dated June 28, 1937, records a submission from the Navy Department transmitting a copy of a Naval Attaché report regarding courtesies and privileges extended to officers of the Japanese cruiser Ashigara during their port call at Kiel. The second entry references Naval Attaché Germany Report #R-361 of May 27, 1937, concerning visits of Japanese naval vessels to German ports, including a cross-reference notation.
